headline: High: Copilot can write and modify repo files while Cognee ingests sensitive support data, creating default-path leakage and cascading-error risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Copilot reads editor buffers and repo context, and Cognee handles documents, workflows, and support history. If Cognee outputs are copied into files or buffers that Copilot consumes, prompt-like content can steer Copilot. Cognee’s session memory and Copilot’s editor integration make the bridge plausible, though not directly documented.
conditions: IF Cognee output is pasted into files or editor buffers that Copilot reads
IF Copilot is asked to summarize or transform Cognee-generated text without provenance filtering
mitigations: Keep Cognee outputs in a separate workspace from Copilot buffers
Prefix imported Cognee text with a non-executable delimiter
Review Copilot suggestions before accepting edits
Disable automatic ingestion of copied notes into coding files
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to Cognee exports

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cognee touches personal data, finance data, and support history, while Copilot reads repo context and sends it to api.githubcopilot.com. If sensitive Cognee content enters shared editor buffers or repo files, Copilot can transmit it off-host. The pair therefore has a realistic default-path leakage risk, even though the exact bridge is indirect.
conditions: IF sensitive Cognee data is placed into files or buffers visible to Copilot
IF Copilot Chat or Workspace is used on those files
mitigations: Do not place support or finance data in Copilot-visible files
Use a separate non-Copilot editor for sensitive notes
Restrict Copilot to sanitized repositories only
Review workspace scope before enabling Chat or Workspace
requires-engineering: enforce DLP/redaction on editor buffers

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cognee supports multiple instances with tenant isolation, while Copilot can write files and modify git state. Both can touch the same repository artifacts, so concurrent edits can conflict even without shell access. The conflict is plausible in default developer workflows, though not guaranteed.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or workspace
IF Copilot Workspace applies edits while Cognee also writes related artifacts
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate branch or workspace
Pause one agent before accepting the other’s edits
Use git status before merging generated changes
Keep Cognee outputs read-only until reviewed
requires-engineering: add locking around shared repo writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: Copilot Workspace can propose and apply edits, and Cognee produces decisions, workflows, and schema structures. If Copilot treats Cognee output as authoritative, errors can cascade into committed code or workflow changes. The pair lacks a built-in verification step in the profiles, so the unsafe path is credible.
conditions: IF Copilot is fed Cognee-generated decisions or workflow text
IF the resulting edits are accepted without human verification
mitigations: Require human review for every Copilot-applied edit
Cross-check Cognee outputs against source data
Use a checklist for any generated workflow change
Limit Copilot to suggestions, not auto-apply
requires-engineering: add validation gates before commit

E_compliance.rationale: Cognee explicitly touches personal data and finance data, while Copilot sends editor context to GitHub/Microsoft services. That creates a plausible residency and processing mismatch for regulated support data. Because the profiles do not show a DPA or residency controls, uncertainty pushes this to high rather than medium.
conditions: IF regulated support or finance data is present in Copilot-visible context
IF organizational policy requires residency or processor restrictions not covered by GitHub Copilot
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from Copilot-visible files
Confirm a DPA and residency terms before use
Restrict Copilot to non-sensitive repositories
Document approved data classes for Copilot
requires-engineering: route sensitive workflows to a compliant environment
